name: SmartSuite
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Configure records, views, automations, and dashboards for one team

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Minimum 3 users; unlimited solutions; 5,000 records/solution; 50 GB storage; 30-day recycle-bin retention.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Minimum 5 users; unlimited solutions; 100,000 records/solution; 100 GB storage; 45-day recycle-bin retention.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 400,000 records/solution; 500 GB storage; 60-day recycle-bin retention; SSO, SCIM and audit controls.

tiers.name: Signature
tiers.limits: Custom capacity and controls; the public page exposes no numeric plan limits.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier; 14-day Professional trial with no card and no automatic charge
pricing.billingTerms: Team and Professional offer monthly + annual billing; annual plans are prepaid; Enterprise and Signature are quote-based
pricing.hiddenCosts: Team has a 3-seat minimum and Professional a 5-seat minimum; a HIPAA BAA requires an annual commitment of at least 25 Professional, 20 Enterprise or 10 Signature seats; invoice payment on Enterprise requires an undisclosed minimum fee.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For SmartSuite, configure records, views, automations, and dashboards for one team. The hard boundary is template breadth, workflow, integrations, permissions, and hosted collaboration, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Model structured records for one team, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, add automations and dashboards, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: template breadth, workflow, integrations, permissions, and hosted collaboration
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for SmartSuite because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: Records, views, forms, automations, and a small dashboard-style app builder; the free limits are visible and sane.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks SmartSuite's polished operational solution templates, dashboarding, granular permissions, and integrated work-management experience.

alternatives.name: Fibery Free
alternatives.desc: Relational records, views, formulas, docs, automations, and dashboards for up to ten users.

facts.engines: Fibery AI is vendor-managed; the free plan includes limited AI/automation credits, but Fibery does not publish a fixed underlying model list for the free plan
facts.dataFormat: Workspace databases, documents, whiteboards, and files live in Fibery's cloud; a full-space export produces Markdown, CSV, and file folders
facts.gapVsPaid: Fibery can model almost anything, but it is harder for a nontechnical team to configure and lacks SmartSuite's ready-made operational solution polish.

alternatives.name: SeaTable Free
alternatives.desc: A serious grid with 10,000 rows, forms, automations, scripts, and an app builder before it asks for money.

facts.dataFormat: Bases live in SeaTable Cloud and can be exported as proprietary .dtable containers containing JSON plus an asset folder; individual tables or views export to XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: SeaTable is primarily a data grid and offers weaker dashboards, integrated work-management templates, and process-oriented permissions than SmartSuite.

alternatives.name: Stackby Free
alternatives.desc: A smaller operational tracker with views, interfaces, linked API columns, and 100 monthly automations.

facts.engines: AI co-builder is available with low free usage; AI fields/agents require paid plans and can connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google Gemini using user-supplied keys
facts.dataFormat: Stacks and attachments live in Stackby cloud; individual tables/views export to CSV and complete stacks can export to Excel
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free workspace is much narrower and its dashboards, permissions, reporting, and workflow depth do not approach SmartSuite's team operating system.

alternatives.name: Teable Free
alternatives.desc: An Airtable-shaped database with 1,000 rows, 100 automations, and a real app builder on the free plan.

facts.engines: Vendor-hosted AI and App Builder features use Teable's configured model services and free-plan credits; the exact model roster can change
facts.dataFormat: Bases, records, attachments, automation state, and app definitions live in Teable Cloud; bases can be backed up as .tea files and tables exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable reproduces the relational records but not SmartSuite's polished dashboards, solution templates, process controls, and broader team-management layer.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SmartSuite Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: There is no free plan now: the pricing page offers a 14-day trial, then paid plans with three-seat minimums.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Team plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for SmartSuite in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: model structured records for one team, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, add automations and dashboards, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
